_note: Topics per persona (PRD §3 stage 3, AGCTM-12). The topic/role relation is many-to-many: PRD §3 says Kata generates relevant *topics* from context x persona, and the 0:55 team quiz already asks the whole team a concept that belongs to one role's topic. The seeded assignments stay mostly one-per-role so the 0:10 narration stays simple; the shape no longer requires it. A topic is a named subgraph of the course in 2-curriculum/concepts.json — its own concept set plus the prerequisite and related edges that fall inside it. It is deliberately NOT a separate course: one acyclic graph means prerequisite gating still works across topics, and `concepts`/`prerequisite_edges` here load into the core's `concept` and `concept_edge` tables unchanged. `bridges_out` records edges that leave the topic, so a topic is never mistaken for a closed world.

_fields.entry_concept: where a learner with no review history starts; always the shallowest concept in the topic
_fields.grounded_in: seed artifacts in 1-context/ that justify this topic existing. A topic with no grounding is a generic curriculum and fails KAT-C1
_fields.bridges_out: edges from a topic concept to a concept outside the topic — the reason topics are subgraphs, not courses
_fields.personas: the roles this topic is for — many-to-many with `roles` in 0-team/personas.json. A topic can serve several roles (the ledger migration is the tech lead's and both seniors'), and a role can hold several topics; `roles[].topics` is the same relation from the other side and the two must agree.

topics.title: Retrying a payment without charging twice
topics.why_this_role_this_week: Sprint 42's theme is 'stop double-charging'. Four of the six juniors have an issue in that cluster, and the code an agent writes for it looks correct either way — the difference is invisible until an incident.

topics.title: Detecting provider drift before the provider tells you
topics.why_this_role_this_week: The seniors review the PRs, and an agent-written adapter passes a suite recorded against fixtures nobody re-records. Adyen changed a response field in August and the connector swallowed it for nine days.

topics.title: The 1 October SCA change, and the engineering under it
topics.why_this_role_this_week: Shane is writing the merchant comms for a regulatory change nobody else on the team can explain — and is shipping agent-written code alongside it. The topic carries an engineering spine (idempotency, money) on purpose: the PM failure mode is vibe-coding without one, so a topic that is only regulatory would leave it intact.

topics.title: Evolving a live ledger
topics.why_this_role_this_week: The migration was reverted on Tuesday after locking `postings` for 34 seconds in staging, and PAY-1875 — the dry-run harness — is the tech lead's own issue. This is the topic where approving a plausible-looking agent design costs the most.

topics.title: Which constraints are real: mandated, technical, or ours
topics.why_this_role_this_week: The SCA change on 1 October moves the challenge step, and PAY-1852 puts retry state in front of the customer for the first time. Both are flows where the designer will be told 'we can't do that' — and needs to know when that is true.
